title: Anisa: a freehold double-storey terrace beside Serenia City's park.
excerpt: A newly handed-over 22 by 70 ft individual-title terrace in an early Serenia City phase, walking distance to a large community park and shops. Sean likes the setting, the developer and the house, but not the neighbour-driven extensions, the concrete lanes or the distance from KL.
takeaways: A 1,951 sq ft, four-bedroom, four-bathroom intermediate unit on a 22 by 70 ft lot, freehold.
Intermediate units list from about RM730,000 to RM780,000, and the unit Sean viewed was being let for close to RM3,800 a month.
Individual title with a guardhouse run by a residents' association, so no pool or gym, but a community park within walking distance.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Anisa is one of the earlier phases of Serenia City, the one buyers queued for at launch. It is a freehold double-storey terrace under individual title rather than strata: after handover the developer builds a guardhouse and residents form an association that charges a monthly fee for security only, with no pool, gym or clubhouse to maintain. Owners can renovate without management approval, and many corner units were already extended a few months after the keys were handed over.

The scheme keeps far more open space than the usual minimum. Wide green buffers separate the first and last rows from the roads and the highway, rows that would otherwise face a junction are replaced by linear parks and concrete lanes between houses, back lanes have covered drains and plenty of street lights, and a basketball court and playgrounds sit within the precinct.

Sean viewed a 22 by 70 ft intermediate unit of 1,951 sq ft with four bedrooms and four bathrooms. The ground floor has a 3.07 m-high living and dining area, a dry kitchen about 4.4 m long, a 3.4 m square bedroom and a large, step-free bathroom with a ramp. Upstairs, a family hall lit by a skylight leads to two identical en-suite bedrooms at the back and a 4.67 by 4.52 m master suite at the front. The car porch is columnless, with an EV-ready plug point and a parcel box.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: Serenia City sits where the North-South Expressway, which runs to KL and the airport, meets the Putrajaya–Cyberjaya Expressway, which leads to Puchong. Planes from the airport are a frequent sight. Anisa itself is next to a large community park with a lake, toddler and children's play areas, a watchtower and basketball and football courts, with a commercial area across from it, all within walking distance. Getting to central KL is still a long trip, and the expressway to Puchong can jam at peak hours.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: On listing platforms, intermediate units sell for about RM730,000 to RM780,000 and corner units for about RM980,000 to RM1 million. After its makeover the unit was offered for rent at RM4,000 a month and was being negotiated at RM3,800. Sean works out that a launch buyer who paid a little over RM800,000 after a 10% discount, with a loan of around RM700,000 to RM750,000, could see rent close to or above the monthly instalment, which he calls rare for a brand-new landed home.

standout.title: Green space the developer could have built on
standout.body: Sean keeps pointing at land that could have taken another two rows of houses: wide buffers in front of and behind the rows, linear parks where homes would face a junction, and a large public park built before the township is finished. Space like that lowers the developer's yield per acre but gives residents privacy, distance from the roads, and somewhere to walk to.

pros: Anisa's place in the master plan: walking distance to a well-equipped community park and to the commercial area in front, so residents can walk instead of drive.
The developer: a large builder running many townships at once, with a track record that makes completion predictable and public infrastructure like the park and amenities paid for up front.
The house itself: a predictable, practical terrace refined over decades of building them, with little to pick on.
cons: Individual title means no pool, gym or clubhouse, and you can't control what neighbours build: once they add canopies or extensions, you may have to follow to keep rainwater out of your porch.
Some design elements, especially the concrete lanes between rows meant for children cycling, will most likely become parking, since there are no dedicated visitor bays.
The location is still some distance from central KL, and highway traffic depends on the time of day.

closing: A freehold landed home with a park at its door, for buyers who would rather have open space and walkability than condo facilities, and can live with the commute.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this September 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The unit belongs to a private owner; its furniture, carpentry and kitchen were done by The Makeover Guys, where Sean works, who were also finding it a tenant. Prices are from listing platforms and the rent was still under negotiation at the time of recording.
